missing_requirements.finding: An optional operational report write, flush or close failure replaces an already-caught/reconciled source CaptureError. The original CaptureError and its EOFError cause are absent from the raised exception chain. logic_errors.title: Operational-report I/O can discard the primary source failure
logic_errors.explanation: run_preview catches the original failure into primary and then executes report_stream.write/flush/close directly in finally. An exception from any of these calls escapes before the final raise primary. Because the original exception handler has already ended, the escaping reporting exception has neither the original failure as __cause__ nor as __context__. Real source EOF/native exit7 plus report write, flush and close faults each reproduce this; the no-report-fault control preserves the original CaptureError and EOFError cause. The native stderr tail still reaches stderr and every owned capture/detector/window resource is closed in these probes. This finding is not a successful-return/terminal-misclassification claim, a lost-all-diagnostics claim, or a surviving-child claim.
logic_errors.required_change: Treat operational report serialization/write/flush/close failures as secondary finalization failures when a primary already exists; retain them as chained/attached diagnostics without replacing that primary. If reporting is the first failure, keep its nonzero failure rather than suppressing it. Still attempt the report close and all other owned cleanup, and add deterministic regressions for write/flush/close failure plus a source or detector primary, with healthy controls. Do not persist arbitrary exception text into the structured report.
